title: Strict-local models with a separably closed coefficient field and algebraic residue extensions
statement: Let $K$ be a field, let $Y$ be a scheme of finite type over $K$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $\bar y$ be a geometric point with underlying point $y$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. Put $b=\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(y)$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree], [def-weil-residue-field], and $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y,\bar y}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. There exist an affine open neighbourhood $U$ of $y$ in $Y$, a separably closed field extension $L/K$ with $\operatorname{trdeg}_K L=b$ [def-kun-separably-closed], and a small cofiltered inverse system (the opposite index category is filtered as defined in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]) $(V_i\to U)$ of nonempty affine schemes with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism] over $U$ [def-pc-scheme], such that each $V_i$ is of finite type over $L$, the maps $V_i\to U$ are $K$-morphisms, and $S\cong\varprojlim_i V_i$ over $U$ (that is, the compatible maps $S\to V_i$ are universal among compatible cones). For every $i$ and every point $v\in V_i$ with image $u\in U$, the induced extension $\kappa(v)/\kappa(u)$ is algebraic (each element satisfies a nonzero polynomial over $\kappa(u)$).

source.place: Tag 0F0U, lemma-strictly-henselian, proof with compatible etale models; Tag 0F0X, lemma-interlude-I, second paragraph (refined residue-field-control input)

proof.text: Choose a finite-type affine chart $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}A_0$ containing $y$, using the finite affine cover in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. If $\mathfrak p_0$ represents $y$, then $\kappa(y)=\operatorname{Frac}(A_0/\mathfrak p_0)$ is finitely generated as a field over $K$: the images of a finite list of $K$-algebra generators generate its fraction field. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-generated-field-finite-transcendence-basis] to obtain a finite basis $\bar t_1,\ldots,\bar t_b$; its size is $b$ by [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Write these elements as fractions of images of elements of $A_0$ and invert the product of their denominators, which is not in $\mathfrak p_0$. This gives a principal affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $y$, still finite type over $K$ (adjoin one inverse), with lifts $t_1,\ldots,t_b\in A$. The map $R=K[T_1,\ldots,T_b]\to A$, $T_i\mapsto t_i$, is injective: a polynomial in its kernel vanishes on the algebraically independent $\bar t_i$. The image of $y$ in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is the generic point, and its residue field is $F=K(T_1,\ldots,T_b)$.

source.place: Tag 0F0U, lemma-strictly-henselian, proof and footnote; Tag 0F0X, lemma-interlude-I, second paragraph

proof.text: Write $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ and let $\bar\eta$ be its image in $\operatorname{Spec}R$. Let $L$ be the separable algebraic closure of $F$ inside $\Omega$, as in [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure]; it is a separably closed algebraic extension of $F$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-ring-triples](3) with the identity affine chart of $\operatorname{Spec}R$. It identifies the pointed-neighbourhood ring colimit with the etale residue-triple colimit, compatibly with the coprojections. The strict henselization of $R$ at $\bar\eta$ is therefore $L$: apply [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples] with prime $(0)$ and residue field $F$. Its colimit is a local ring whose maximal ideal is $(0)$ and whose residue field is $L$, so the residue quotient is the ring itself. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](3) to $U\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ to obtain a unital $K$-algebra map $h:L\to B=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y,\bar y}$ compatible with $R\to A\to B$. The same functoriality statement (1) makes $B$ a nonzero local ring, so $h$ is injective. To identify the ring over $U$ with the required ring over $Y$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-ring-triples](2) to the affine chart $U\subset Y$. The affine pointed neighbourhoods factoring through $U$ give the same ring colimit as all affine pointed neighbourhoods of $Y$; as pointed $U$-neighbourhoods they are precisely the diagram defining $\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{U,\bar y}$. The identification respects the coprojections, in particular the map from $A$ and the geometric residue embedding. Thus $B$ and its $A$-structure are the requested ones. Finally, [lem-kun-transcendence-degree-tower] gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_K L=\operatorname{trdeg}_K F=b$, since $L/F$ is algebraic.

source.place: Tag 0F0U, lemma-strictly-henselian, proof and footnote; Tag 0F0X, lemma-interlude-I, second paragraph

proof.text: Use [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] for the two pointed affine schemes $\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $U$ to choose small filtered ring diagrams $D:I\to\mathbf{CRing}$ and $E:J\to\mathbf{CRing}$ with $L=\varinjlim_iD_i$ and $B=\varinjlim_jE_j$. The maps $R\to D_i$ and $A\to E_j$ are etale, and both diagrams and their colimits are over $R$. Choose the representative subcategories to include the identity neighbourhoods $D_{i_0}=R$ and $E_{j_0}=A$; these are initial objects in the ring-indexed categories. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine], every $D_i$ is finitely presented over $R$ and every $E_j$ is finitely presented over $A$. In particular $E_j$ is finite type over $K$ and over $R$, because $A$ is finite type over $K$ and the image of $R$ contains $K$.

source.place: Tag 0F0U, lemma-strictly-henselian, proof and footnote; Tag 0F0X, lemma-interlude-I, second paragraph

proof.text: Here is the finite-presentation calculation needed for the compatible models. For any finitely presented $R$-algebra $P=R[X_1,\ldots,X_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ and any $R$-algebra map $P\to B$, [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise](1) lifts the images of the $X_r$ into some $E_j$. Move finitely many representatives to a common object using filteredness. Evaluate the finitely many relations there; their images in $B$ are zero. Part (2) of the same node and filteredness move these equalities to one later object, giving an $R$-algebra map $P\to E_k$ factoring the original map. Two maps from a finitely generated $R$-algebra to stages of $E$ that induce the same map to $B$ agree after a common refinement: apply part (2) to their finitely many generator images and combine the finitely many equalities. If the resulting witnesses give different arrows out of a stage, equalize those arrows using filteredness, so that all equalities use the same transition. This calculation uses the full small filtered category $J$, not an assumed directed poset.

source.place: Tag 0F0U, lemma-strictly-henselian, proof and footnote; Tag 0F0X, lemma-interlude-I, second paragraph

proof.text: Define a small category $T$ whose objects are triples $\tau=(i,j,\psi)$ with $\psi:D_i\to E_j$ an $R$-algebra map satisfying $\beta_j\psi=h\alpha_i$, where $\alpha_i:D_i\to L$ and $\beta_j:E_j\to B$ are the coprojections. A morphism to $(i',j',\psi')$ is a pair $(a:i\to i',c:j\to j')$ with $E(c)\psi=\psi'D(a)$. It is small because $I,J$ are small and each set of ring maps is a set. It is nonempty: $(i_0,j_0,R\to A)$ is an object. To give a successor of two triples, first choose a common $i'$ in $I$. Apply the finite-presentation calculation of step 4 to $D_{i'}\to L\xrightarrow h B$ to obtain a lift into some $E_k$. Choose a common successor in $J$ of $k$ and the two old $j$'s. The composites from each old $D_i$ to that stage and to $B$ agree; the eventual-equality calculation of step 4, applied to the finite generators of both old $D_i$, gives a further stage where both compatibility squares commute. For two parallel arrows of triples, equalize their $I$ components by $i'\to i''$ and their $J$ components by $j'\to j''$. Lift $D_{i''}\to B$ to a stage of $E$ and then refine $j''$ so that its restriction along $D_{i'}\to D_{i''}$ agrees with the old $\psi'$; step 4 gives precisely this equality. The resulting morphism out of the target triple equalizes the original pair in both components. These are all three filteredness axioms of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Tag 0F0U, lemma-strictly-henselian, proof and footnote; Tag 0F0X, lemma-interlude-I, second paragraph

proof.text: For $\tau=(i,j,\psi)$ put $C_\tau=E_j\otimes_{D_i,\psi}L$. A morphism $(a,c)$ of triples induces $e\otimes\ell\mapsto E(c)(e)\otimes\ell$; the compatibility square makes this well-defined. The maps $\gamma_\tau:C_\tau\to B$, $e\otimes\ell\mapsto\beta_j(e)h(\ell)$, are compatible unital maps. The ring $C_\tau$ is finite type over $L$: take any finite set of $R$-algebra generators of $E_j$ from step 3; their tensors with $1$ generate $C_\tau$ over $L$. Also $C_\tau$ is nonzero because it maps unitally to the nonzero ring $B$. More explicitly, composing $\gamma_\tau$ with the residue map from $B$ to its residue field gives a unital map to a field; its kernel is a proper prime ideal of $C_\tau$, since a product mapping to zero in a field has a factor mapping to zero. This prime is a point of $V_\tau$, proving nonemptiness without invoking existence of maximal ideals. All these maps preserve the given $A$-algebra structures, hence their spectra are $K$-morphisms over $U$.

source.place: Tag 0F0U, lemma-strictly-henselian, proof and footnote; Tag 0F0X, lemma-interlude-I, second paragraph

proof.text: We verify the colimit, including its universal property, rather than assuming that the $C_\tau$ are subalgebras of $B$. Let $m_\tau:C_\tau\to M$ be any compatible cocone of commutative rings. For every $j$, $(i_0,j,R\to E_j)$ is a triple, so $e\mapsto m_{(i_0,j)}(e\otimes1)$ defines compatible maps $E_j\to M$, and hence a unique ring map $f:B\to M$. The triple $(i_0,j_0)$ maps to every triple, so all restrictions $\ell\mapsto m_\tau(1\otimes\ell)$ are the same map $g:L\to M$. For any $\ell\in L$, [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise](1) gives $d\in D_i$ with $\alpha_i(d)=\ell$; step 4 supplies a triple $(i,j,\psi)$. The tensor relation $\psi(d)\otimes1=1\otimes\alpha_i(d)$ then gives $f(h(\ell))=g(\ell)$. There is a morphism $(i_0,j)\to(i,j,\psi)$, so $m_\tau(e\otimes1)=f(\beta_j(e))$. Since $C_\tau$ is generated as a ring by these elements and $1\otimes L$, these two equations give $m_\tau=f\gamma_\tau$. Uniqueness follows from the colimit presentation $B=\varinjlim E_j$. Thus $B=\varinjlim_T C_\tau$ as rings and as $A$-algebras. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-small-colimit-limit], the compatible maps from $S=\operatorname{Spec}B$ to $V_\tau=\operatorname{Spec}C_\tau$ are a limit cone in schemes; the compatibility with $A$ makes it a limit over $U$ as well.

source.place: Tag 0F0U, lemma-strictly-henselian, proof and footnote; Tag 0F0X, lemma-interlude-I, second paragraph

proof.text: Fix a prime $q$ of $C_\tau$ and let $w$ and $u$ be its contractions to $E_j$ and $A$, respectively. Since $A\to E_j$ is etale, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-residue-field-separable] gives a finite separable extension $\kappa(w)/\kappa(u)$. Let $p_i$ be the kernel of $D_i\to L$. This is also the contraction of $w$ to $D_i$: in $C_\tau/q$ the two images of $D_i$ agree, and the unital map from the field $L$ to $\kappa(q)$ is injective. The induced field embeddings $\kappa(p_i)\to L$ and $\kappa(p_i)\to\kappa(w)$ are therefore compatible in $\kappa(q)$. Since $R\to L$ is injective, $p_i$ contracts to $(0)$ in $R$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-residue-field-separable] to $R\to D_i$ to obtain $\kappa(p_i)/F$ finite separable. In particular $L/\kappa(p_i)$ is algebraic: every polynomial witnessing algebraicity over $F$ also witnesses algebraicity over this intermediate field. The field $\kappa(q)$ is generated by the images of $\kappa(w)$ and $L$, because $C_\tau$ is generated by $E_j$ and $L$ and $\kappa(q)=\operatorname{Frac}(C_\tau/q)$. Consequently $\kappa(q)/\kappa(w)$ is algebraic. Explicitly, any one of its elements is a rational expression in finitely many elements of $L$ with coefficients in $\kappa(w)$; those elements are algebraic over $\kappa(w)$, so their successive simple adjunctions are finite-dimensional fields (use their monic minimal polynomials). The expression belongs to this finite extension. As $\kappa(w)/\kappa(u)$ is finite, the same element is algebraic over $\kappa(u)$: the finite-dimensional tower is finite-dimensional, and its powers are linearly dependent. This proves the required residue algebraicity for every point, without a lifting-to-$S$ assumption.

source.place: Tag 0F0U, lemma-strictly-henselian, proof and footnote; Tag 0F0X, lemma-interlude-I, second paragraph

proof.text: The schemes $V_\tau$ are nonempty by step 6 and are affine and finite type over $L$. Their inverse index category is the small cofiltered category $T^{\mathrm{op}}$ by step 5. Their transition maps are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine], since both their source and target are affine. Thus steps 2, 6, 7 and 8 establish every asserted clause, including the limit over $U$ and every residue extension. When $b=0$ use $R=F=K$ and the empty list of $t_i$; all the constructions and arguments still apply.
